name: Modify system settings
plain: Lets the app change system settings like brightness and ringtone.
meaning: Allows changing display brightness, ringtones and timeouts. A minor privacy risk but often requested.

android.revocation: Settings > Special app access > Modify system settings

ios.note: Apps may set screen brightness only; no other settings.

limits.headline: Can change brightness, ringtone and screen timeout on Android; iPhone allows only brightness
limits.user_action: You switch on Modify system settings for the app in Settings
can: Change the ringtone and screen timeout (Android)
Set brightness on iPhone with no prompt
cannot: Change these on Android before you switch it on in Settings
Change anything but brightness on iPhone
limits.reach_label: A few display and sound settings
limits.differs: Android needs a Settings switch; iPhone allows brightness only, with no prompt.

story.what_it_is: Lets an app change system settings like brightness, ringtone and screen timeout.
story.for_you: The app asks for special access to modify settings. If you allow it, it can change screen brightness or set a ringtone. You will see the change but may not know which app did it.
story.for_makers: Utility apps want to control brightness and sounds. It is a low risk request, but it is often used to look more useful. The permission needs a special screen, not a normal prompt.

use_cases.example: A brightness app lowers the screen for night reading.
A reader app sets a screen timeout so the screen stays on.
A ringtone app sets a song as your ringtone.
A workout app brightens the screen outdoors.
A low vision app makes the screen brighter and text larger.
A game dims the screen to save battery.
A parent app sets sound and screen limits.

story.android_note: A special access screen has been needed since Android 6.
story.ios_note: iPhone apps can only set screen brightness. They cannot change other settings.
